action.message:
I was unable to complete the feature fix. Public regression tests pass, but the actual bug fix was NOT implemented.

What happened:
- I explored the relevant code in `django/db/models/fields/related_lookups.py` (`RelatedIn.get_prep_lookup`, lines 76-109) and `django/db/models/sql/query.py` (`has_select_fields` 267-270, `set_annotation_mask` 2360-2366, `add_annotation` 1109-1119, `annotation_select` 2435-2452).
- Root cause identified: `alias()` calls `add_annotation(select=False)`, which invokes `set_annotation_mask(set(self.annotation_select).difference({alias}))`, converting `annotation_select_mask` from `None` to an explicit set. This makes `has_select_fields` return True, so `RelatedIn.get_prep_lookup` skips `clear_select_clause()`, leaving all columns selected and producing "sub-select returns 10 columns - expected 1".
- However, my edits were erroneous: I accidentally duplicated the `has_select_fields` property and duplicated `set_annotation_mask`, then reverted both. The net result is that the two target files are effectively unchanged from their original state — no functional fix was applied.

Verification status: `scoped_tests` on the `annotations` selection passed (80 tests, returncode 0), but this only reflects the unmodified baseline, not a fix. The feature acceptance test (`test_annotation_and_alias_filter_in_subquery`) was not run and would still fail.

Recommended fix (not applied): make `has_select_fields` not count annotations added via `alias()`. The upstream approach is to have `set_annotation_mask` reset the mask to `None` when it covers all annotations, and/or redefine `has_select_fields` to be based on explicit select fields (`self.select`/`values_select`/`extra_select_mask`) rather than `annotation_select_mask`, so that `RelatedIn.get_prep_lookup` correctly calls `clear_select_clause()`.

I am reporting this honestly as incomplete rather than claiming success.
